subjects.description: small red rectangular block attached to the bottom of a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A red block hangs from a vertical spring and oscillates up and down. The oscillation continues for the whole clip without being started or stopped on camera.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The s channel shows a straight-line oscillation of ~250 pix peak-to-peak with ~0.6 s period and slowly shrinking amplitude, classic mass-on-spring. I propose undamped SHM as baseline, then viscous linear damping, quadratic air drag, and a Duffing nonlinear spring, to compete on decay shape and amplitude-dependent frequency in the held-back 30%.

critique.headline: Spring keeps bouncing with a steady hidden push
critique.revision_idea: Add quadratic air drag on top of linear damping and the steady push. The leftover misses still swing up and down with the motion and are largest when the block moves fastest, which is what speed-squared drag would fix.
critique.why_it_won: It keeps pushing the swing so it does not die out like the plain damped laws, matching the endless bouncing.

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6605630). The round was named in 3bc0190 and pushed before it existed; the law's SHA-256 was pushed in d846c66 before the clip was rendered; the run used commit 0b852c8 on a clean tree; the law was revealed in b1902a4. Missed under the rule, with the drive found. The drawn law was a linear spring with dry (Coulomb) friction and a periodic drive at 13.85 rad/s. The misses of Muse Spark's best law peaked at 13.91 rad/s, 153 times the noise, labelled unexplained, and code added that law plus a drive started there. That law won: drive frequency 13.912 ± 0.047 rad/s against 13.85 (1.3σ), drive strength 3.73 ± 0.22 m/s² against 3.72, natural frequency 10.107 ± 0.073 against 10.114. Its damping is viscous (15σ from zero) where the drawn friction is dry, so the term set differs. Muse Wonder also wrote a driven law (it ranked second, tied, with one more term). The winner misses the unseen frames by 15 times the noise, against 114 for the best law without a drive. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

drawn.equation: x'' = -(k/m) x - mu sign(x') + F0 cos(wd t)
drawn.x: displacement below the resting point (m, down positive); t from release

mu.rule: the swing dies in N half cycles, N uniform in [10, 16] (drawn 10.31); mu = w0^2 A / (2N)

F0.rule: F0 / |w0^2 - wd^2| = share of A uniform in [0.15, 0.35] (drawn 0.330)

wd.rule: wd / w0 uniform in [0.55, 0.8] or [1.25, 1.6], each half the time (drawn 1.369)

sealed.narration: a block on a spring, filmed from the side
sealed.rule: found only if the winner's term set equals the drawn term set, a fitted term whose constant is within 2σ of zero counting as absent, and every shared constant is within 2σ of the drawn value
sealed.terms: winner (code: Muse Spark's law plus a drive at the unexplained residual peak): linear (ω₀), cubic α = 0.00002 ± 0.0002 (0.1σ, absent), viscous γ = 0.71 ± 0.05 (15σ, present), drive F = 2894 ± 170 px/s² (17σ, present) at ω_d = 13.912 ± 0.047; drawn: linear, Coulomb, drive. Term sets differ: viscous where Coulomb was drawn.
